name: field keys follow-up: shelf listing, status line, JU-06A instruments, pad rename

pr.title: Follow up on field keys: list the instruments, add juno and bass, rename the pad, and keep the notes last
pr.head: cdcccaab60aa148d3e2b9ae2afbe7ac2031746c3

summary: field keys turns the computer keyboard into a MIDI source. Given an instrument name, it also plays a SuperCollider program live. A bare name such as pad resolves to shared/instruments/pad.scd, the project's instruments shelf, by the same rule a supercollider: track entry uses. This pull request collects the fixes from the first hands-on testing after the keyboard-instrument work merged in #178 to #182.

• A missing name lists the shelf. Before, field keys bass printed only that the file did not exist. Now the error lists every program on the shelf, split into those that play from notes and those that only render, each by a name field keys accepts.
  • The notes come last on the status line. Playing used to shift everything after the notes. Now the notes end the line, and an instrument's state has a line of its own above it.
  • Two more playable instruments. examples/bloom gains juno and bass, ports of the JU-06A synth from the okamnesiac/offset repository.
  • still-water-pad becomes pad. The example's sine pad gets a shorter name in the example, the docs, and the plan.
  • The keymap reload test stops flaking. It saves again every 500 ms until each reload arrives, because a watch that has just started can lose the first file event.

The review of this head is clean. The one blocking finding from an earlier head, a dotted program listed by a name that did not resolve, is fixed and verified, and every suggestion from the reviews has been taken.

cards.title: Terms this page uses
cards.html:
• Shelf: shared/instruments/, where a bare instrument name resolves.
  • Bare name: a name with no /. instrumentProgram adds .scd to it only when it has no extension at all.
  • Voice mode: a program run with FIELD_MODE=voice. Its value must be a SynthDef that the voice host plays once per note.
  • Render mode: the same program run by a build, writing a WAV file offline.
  • Voice host: the sclang process running sc/voice-host.scd, which plays an instrument live.
  • Status line: the line field keys redraws in place while you play.
  • JU-06A: a SuperCollider model of the Roland Juno's signal chain, from okamnesiac/offset.

groups.title: field keys: the shelf listing and the status line
groups.kicker: A missing name lists the shelf by names that resolve, and the status line ends with the notes
intro: When you name an instrument that is not on the shelf, resolveInstrument still throws, and the CLI still prints the message and exits 1. The message now ends with the shelf's contents. shelfInstruments reads shared/instruments/, keeps regular files whose names end in .scd, and sorts them. It puts a program under plays from notes when its text contains FIELD_MODE, and under renders only otherwise. That shortcut holds because voice is the only value FIELD_MODE takes, and it spares the error from starting sclang once per program.

Each program is listed by a name field keys accepts. Usually that is the file name without .scd. A name that would still have an extension, such as pad.v2, keeps its .scd, because field keys adds .scd only to a name with no extension.
The status line ends with the notes

The status line shows the MIDI source, the keymap, the transpose, the velocity, and any message, then the notes sounding last. Playing changes only the end of the line. When the line is wider than the terminal, statusText shortens the text before the notes and marks the cut with an ellipsis. An instrument's state, such as juno live at 48000 Hz on MacBook Pro Speakers, moves to its own line above. draw writes that line once and rewrites it, by moving the cursor up one line, only when its text changes. The opening Playing … Esc or Ctrl-C quits. line is gone.

checks.text: Only draw writes to the terminal while you play: the MIDI helper and the voice host both run with piped output. So the cursor is always on the status line when draw moves up one line to rewrite the instrument's line.

files.note: resolveInstrument appends the listing, which shelfInstruments builds. draw adds the instrument's line, and statusText puts the notes last and fits the line to a width.

checks.text: The fix for the previous head's finding. Against a scratch shelf, pad.v2.scd lists as pad.v2.scd, a.scd.scd as a.scd.scd, and .hidden.scd as .hidden, and resolveInstrument accepts each listed name.
entry.isFile() is false for a directory named *.scd and for the dangling .#name.scd link Emacs leaves while a buffer is unsaved, so the listing never tries to read either.
Ran field keys organ in examples/bloom with no terminal attached. It exits 1 and prints exactly the listing docs/keys.md shows, before any terminal, MIDI, or sclang work starts.
This branch shortens the notes only when they alone are longer than the width, and the comment above and docs/keys.md now say exactly that.

files.note: New. statusText ends with the notes after a reload error, and a 30-column line keeps the notes whole and cuts the text before them.

groups.title: Two JU-06A instruments in examples/bloom
groups.kicker: juno and bass port offset's Juno model, and each both plays from notes and renders
intro: Before this change, the sine pad was the only example instrument you could play from the keyboard. juno.scd and bass.scd port the JU-06A from the okamnesiac/offset repository. It models the Roland Juno's chain: oscillators (saw, pulse, sub, and noise), a high-pass filter, a resonant low-pass filter, and an amplifier under one ADSR envelope, then a chorus.

Each program answers both modes. In voice mode, its last expression is a SynthDef with the freq, amp, gate, and out controls the voice host sets. The SynthDef writes two channels and frees itself when its envelope ends. In render mode, the program renders a short demo offline: juno holds a C minor ninth chord, and bass plays offset's eight-note line.

The two files repeat the same ju06a function on purpose. A program's own bytes are the cache key for what it renders. A shared file loaded at run time could change the sound without invalidating the renders that used it.

checks.text: The review did not start sclang, so nothing here was rendered or played. The pull request body reports that both renders peak below 0 dBFS and repeat byte for byte with a fixed seed.

files.note: The classic Juno pad: saw and pulse with the pulse width swept, a slow attack, a long release, and the chorus on.

checks.text: Compared every knob with the "Classic Juno pad" in offset's sessions/juno.scd, and the ju06a graph with offset's patches/ju06a.scd, by reading both. They match.
The chord's note-offs are added between its note-ons, out of time order. Score sorts its events when it is built, so the order does not matter.

files.note: offset's bass: one saw, a square sub an octave down, a filter the envelope opens on each note, and no chorus. It plays at true pitch.

checks.text: Compared every knob with the ~ju06a factory defaults in offset's patches/ju06a.scd, by reading both. They match.

groups.title: still-water-pad becomes pad
groups.kicker: The example's sine pad gets a shorter name everywhere except the plan's records of past runs
intro: shared/instruments/still-water-pad.scd moves to pad.scd, and its two SynthDefs become padKey and padVoice. The creek track pad-sc now names source: pad.scd, and the docs, the example's README, the repository README, and the keyboard-instrument plan use the new name.
The plan's verification tables in §10.3 and §13.3 keep the old name, because those rows record runs made under it. A new note in §13.2 says so.
A render's cache key includes the program's bytes, and the rename changes them, so pad-sc renders once more on its next build.

checks.text: git grep still-water-pad finds only the plan's §10.3 and §13.3 rows and the note about them. field check in examples/bloom, the step CI runs, prints ok.

files.note: Renamed from still-water-pad.scd. Only the header comment and the two SynthDef names change.
The render entry names the renamed program.
Follows the rename, and states the .scd rule as the code applies it: .scd is added to a name with no extension.

The plan is in-progress, so its design text and acceptance criteria follow the new name, and §2.1, §2.4, and criterion 25 describe the instrument's own line. §13.2 gains the note about the rows that keep the old name.

checks.text: Criterion 25 now looks for the restart on the instrument's line, which is where draw writes it.

groups.title: The keymap reload test stops flaking
groups.kicker: The test saves again until each reload arrives, because a watch just started can lose the first event
intro: watchKeymap reloads a keymap file when you save it, by watching the file's directory. Its test saves three times and checks each reload. Under load, the test failed now and then with no reload 1 within 5 s. The first save's event was sometimes lost outright, because the test saves right after it starts the watch, and the macOS directory watch is not yet live.

saveUntilReload now saves again every 500 ms until the expected reload arrives. A repeat cannot add a reload, because watchKeymap reloads only when the file's text differs from what it last loaded. The test's budget is 20 s, enough for three reloads of up to 5 s each.

files.note: saveUntilReload replaces nextReload, and each of the three edits goes through it.

checks.text: Ran this file 32 times, eight at a time, at 8b9718d, whose test code this head keeps: all passed, where 3 of 8 failed at 8447be4. At least 5 runs took over 500 ms, so they reached the re-save and recovered through it.
